newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten tells Hong Kong to look beyond handover.
newsitem.headline: Patten tells Hong Kong to look beyond handover.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten has called on the territory to look forward instead of remembering the past as the colony prepares to return to Chinese rule in just 45 days.

Patten, whose governorship ceases at midnight on June 30 when Britain hands Hong Kong back to China ending more than 150 years of colonial rule, made the remarks in the first chapter of the 1997 edition of Hong Kong Government yearbook, received by Reuters late on Friday.

"Looking back at history can be an uncomfortable experience at the best of times, but the dangers come not from forgetting but from making history a tool of ideology, from attempts to rectify a past that is already fixed, rather than to respond open-heartedly to what the present has to offer, to welcome reconciliation and the building of new things," he said.

"When the convenient paper target of the last veneer of colonial rule is peeled away with my departure at midnight on June 30, there is an opportunity to look afresh at what lies underneath," he said.
"And what is that? Not some seething pot of repressed ambitions, conflicting ideologies and burning grievances, but a mature, well-balanced society."

Patten has been constantly criticised by China and pro-China newspapers in Hong Kong during his five-year tenure because of his introduction of democratic reforms in the territory despite Beijing's protests.
